item.title: US Senate advances major bill boosting energy infrastructure
item.description:
On Monday evening, the Senate moved one step closer to passing the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) with a 73–25 procedural vote to bring the bill to the floor for the full chamber to consider. Sponsored by Sen. Shelley Moore Capito (R–W.Va.), chairwoman of the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee, the 494-page bill would modify the federal permitting process by limiting the scope of environmental reviews and expediting the timeline for project approval. The federal permitting process has stifled development in America's energy, housing, and transportation industries for decades. The average timeline to complete an environmental impact statement—the most stringent review under the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA)—is over two years, according to a 2025 report by the White House Council on Environmental Quality. The bill would address this challenge…

item.title: Firing Hegseth
item.description:
Impeach the man: Yesterday, Rep. Thomas Massie (R–Ky.) introduced articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. "Massie has alleged that the war is unconstitutional, because the Trump administration launched the conflict without the approval of lawmakers and has since continued military action despite Congress demanding that the Pentagon cease hostilities," reports The Washington Post. Massie has long opposed executive abuse of warmaking powers and has frequently admonished his colleagues to serve as legitimate checks on the president, specifically when it comes to foreign policy. item.title: Lawsuit quickly follows Washington ballot measure on trans sports participation
item.description:
A coalition of parents, educators and nonprofit organizations sued the state of Washington late Monday over a recently passed ballot initiative banning transgender girls from competing on girls’ K-12 sports teams, arguing that the measure, which is set to take effect next month, conflicts with the state’s own constitution. Washington voters approved the initiative, IL26-638 , in last week’s midterms with roughly 56 percent of the vote, according to Decision Desk HQ. Similar initiatives restricting trans student-athletes’ participation in sports passed in Arizona, Nebraska and Colorado. But unlike those measures, which broadly compel schools to designate athletic teams as exclusively male, female or co-ed, Washington’s initiative applies to only girls’ sports . It’s also the only law of its kind requiring students to verify their sex assigned at birth — through either genetic or hormone…

item.title: French police raid Ritz hotel in Mohamed Al Fayed sexual abuse investigation
item.description:
Arrests made after three properties were searched in relation to inquiry into late businessman French police have made arrests after raiding three properties, including the Ritz hotel in Paris , in relation to an investigation into sexual abuse and trafficking by Mohamed Al Fayed. Several individuals were taken into custody for questioning last month and later released, according to the Paris public prosecutor’s office.
